A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AlignDistil and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–E. The added material and relocated content can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original alignment evaluations in Table 1, reward and extrapolation ablations in Tables 2–3, and convergence experiments in Figure 2.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds TL;DR training and evaluation results in Table 4.

M1.justification: The contrastive DPO reward, adaptive logit extrapolation, and on-policy/off-policy distillation objectives remain unchanged. The TL;DR experiment applies the existing method with task-specific settings.

E1.justification: Section 6.3 and Appendix C.2 add one focused coverage extension: dedicated TL;DR summarization training and evaluation using its SFT and preference datasets. UltraFeedback and the three original alignment benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: The new TL;DR comparison includes an explicitly trained SFT-only baseline, also used as the win-rate reference. DPO, PPO, and RTO are reused comparators; the original Table 1 comparator roster is unchanged.

E3.justification: The added TL;DR protocol starts from Qwen2.5-1.5B-Base, performs SFT before alignment, and evaluates 1,000 randomly sampled validation items. It reports Qwen2.5-72B-judged wins against SFT and average scores from the PPO reward model. Existing experimental protocols are retained.

E4.justification: The reward ablation, extrapolation sensitivity study, convergence comparison, and appendix judge evaluation retain their evidence. TL;DR adds benchmark results rather than a new ablation or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. The new TL;DR results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: New Table 4 reports TL;DR win rates/rewards of 92.8%/2.28 for off-policy AlignDistil and 92.5%/2.46 for on-policy AlignDistil, versus 87.7%/2.22 for PPO and 90.8%/1.98 for RTO. These are additional results under a new setting; existing tables and convergence findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 1, the method equations, and derivations in Appendices A, B, and E are unchanged. Correcting the Section 4.1 reference from Equation 22 to Equation 11 changes navigation, not mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims about RLHF–distillation equivalence, the two method components, alignment performance, and faster convergence. TL;DR supplies additional support without redefining these claims.

C2.justification: Section 6.1 adds doubled trainable reward-model capacity as an explanation for the existing contrastive reward result. The TL;DR discussion attributes PPO/RTO reward-score differences to their different optimization targets. The limitation to approximately 1.5B models remains unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C.2 adds dataset access references, SFT and reward-model training budgets, alignment hyperparameters, and evaluation details. However, both r = 1 and r = 2 are labeled Off-Policy AlignDistil, leaving their intended assignment to the two variants ambiguous.

R1.justification: v2 adds Ahmadian et al. (2024) for the evaluation prompt and Zhang et al. (2025) to the distillation discussion. The added Stiennon preprint entry overlaps the already cited summarization work. The broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds a TL;DR subsection and acknowledgments, divides Appendix C into dataset-specific subsections, updates affiliations, and makes limited wording and cross-reference corrections. Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds TL;DR Table 4 and moves the unchanged convergence Figure 2 from page 7 to page 8. The appendix evaluator table becomes Table 5 and shifts position. Existing figure content, table designs, and the document template remain intact.

improvement.justification: The TL;DR experiment and Appendix C.2 strengthen empirical breadth through a separate summarization training setup and document its evaluation. This is a limited improvement: the original theory and evidence remain unchanged, evaluation still covers approximately 1.5B models without uncertainty estimates, and duplicate off-policy labels obscure the new r settings.
